text:
sasha: heads up — small-batch p95 jumped ~3.2x after the gateway + fused-matmul merge (sha abc1234). Canary at 14:12 UTC shows clear delta right after the deploy.

omar: ack, can you drop the perf numbers? short vs long seq?

sasha: shortseq (seq=32, batch=1) p95: 28ms -> 90ms. longseq (seq=512) no noticeable change. KV hit rate for these short requests dropped from ~92% to ~60% on the affected hosts.

lee: hmm that points to a cache-prefetch interaction. Which code landed in abc1234? I remember a prefetch change in fused path.

sasha: yes — the commit enabled prefetching in fused_matmul_forward to reduce latency for large batches. profiler snippet from a reproduced run below: 

```
flamegraph sample:
decode_loop  100ms
 - fused_matmul_forward  55ms  <-- increased
   - prefetch_kv_async  18ms
   - cudaMemcpyAsync(kv_buf) 14ms
 - kv_lookup  20ms
 - softmax  10ms
```

sasha: the extra async memcopies are interleaving with short decode tails and causing GPU H2D contention.

nora: can we reproduce locally in CI? James, can you run the perf harness with the shortseq config?

james: running now: `./scripts/run_perf --model=gpt-small --seq=32 --batch=1 --iters=2000 --trace=perf.json`

bench-bot: result from james (run-id 2026-03-20T15:30): p95=88ms, p50=22ms, kv_hit=61% (baseline p95=27ms). Attached perf.json (link).

infra-bot: canary autoscaler observed more queueing but no host OOMs. No infra-level anomalies.

omar: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) disable prefetch in fused_matmul for short sequences via env var (REDWOOD_PREFETCH_FUSED=0), 2) force fallback to legacy matmul kernel for short batches (REDWOOD_FORCE_LEGACY_MATMUL=1). Which is quick to flip?

lee: REDWOOD_PREFETCH_FUSED is already wired in runtime flags, flipping it is a safe canary change. FORCE_LEGACY is a bit gnarlier but possible.

sasha: I'll flip REDWOOD_PREFETCH_FUSED=0 on the canary pool and rerun james' harness.

(sasha updates the canary)

james: rerun complete: p95=30ms, p50=23ms, kv_hit=90%. Looks much better.

nora: great — that isolates prefetch in fused path as the likely culprit. We should still do a bisect to the exact hunk in abc1234.

omar: agree. @sasha can you capture the minimal repro and run git bisect between last-good sha def7890 and abc1234? If it's just prefetch flag behavior we can ship a targeted revert or gating.

sasha: starting git bisect now. I already have a failing test run script. Will report back with candidate commit.

lee: long term we need a microbenchmark for prefetch vs no-prefetch on short-batch tail latency. Add to perf-suite so CI catches this.

james: filing a short-run perf job (shortseq, batch=1) as a required gate for runtime merges. PR coming.

bench-bot: created job `perf/shortseq-p95` and queued against main.

infra-bot: FYI I've added a temporary canary tag to avoid rollout to all hosts until bisect is done.

sasha: bisect result: commit abc1234: change in fused_matmul -> added prefetch_kv_async() when microbatch < 4. Patch: `if (microbatch >= 4) prefetch_kv_async()` accidentally inverted condition.

omar: wow, inverted logic explains why short microbatch hit the prefetch path. Oops. That should be a one-line revert.

lee: propose: revert the faulty conditional and push a test asserting prefetch only on `microbatch>=4`. Add an inline comment explaining the rationale.

nora: create a rollback PR and mark canary hold until merged. We'll also keep REDWOOD_PREFETCH_FUSED=0 until the PR lands.

sasha: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/commit/revert-abc1234 (link). Rolling out to canary now.

james: smoke looks good on canary after revert. p95 back to baseline.

omar: nice catch everyone. Follow-ups: 1) add perf gate job (james), 2) add unit test for prefetch conditional (lee), 3) retro note in release notes about fused prefetch behavior (sasha).

sasha: adding retro and postmortem draft. Thanks. :thumbsup:

lee: :thumbsup:

nora: :100:
